carriers.support: the cardinality of the outcome space (vocabulary, legal-move count, label set)
carriers.n: the number of observations the figure is computed over
carriers.dim: the dimension of the space the quantity lives in
carriers.base_rate: the prevalence of the positive class, or the pre-edit value being ratio'd
carriers.selection: how many candidates a max or best-of was taken over
carriers.bound: whether the measure is bounded, so it compresses near its ceiling or floor

efficacy_p_gt_0.5.what: fraction of cases whose target probability exceeds 0.5 over the WHOLE vocabulary
support: mass spreads over more tokens as the vocabulary grows, so the same concentration reads lower
base_rate: a target already near 0.5 before the edit needs less to cross than one near 0
bound: a hard threshold on a bounded quantity: once every case is over 0.5 the measure cannot report further improvement, which is the saturation this lane hit at every edit-set size

efficacy_legal_renormalised.what: the same threshold after renormalising over the LEGAL moves at that position
support: the vocabulary is divided out; what remains is the legal-move count, which varies by POSITION and not by rung, so it averages out across a rung rather than trending with it
bound: still a hard threshold, so it still saturates

support: beating 16 competitors is harder than beating 9, though the dependence is weaker than a threshold on raw probability

competence_set_valued.what: fraction of positions whose argmax lies IN the optimal set
support: 'did it pick a correct move' means the same at every board size; this is why it is the cross-rung damage measure
n: a fraction, with its denominator reported
base_rate: measured against the oracle, not against the model's own previous answer
bound: bounded above by 1, so it compresses near a competent net

damage_tv.what: mean total variation between parent and child move distributions
support: bounded in [0,1] and compresses as the distribution spreads over a bigger board
n: a mean over positions, denominator reported

damage_kl.what: mean KL at the read position
support: unbounded, and its typical magnitude grows with the support it sums over - in the OPPOSITE direction to TV, which is why neither is safe across rungs

crowding_fraction_c_over_a.what: mean of c/a over the edit's keys
dim: a ratio of two quantities in the same space, so the ridge scale cancels; this is the lane's reason for using the RATIO rather than c alone
n: crowding rises with the NUMBER OF KEYS, so it is only comparable at a fixed edit count - which the ladder holds fixed on purpose
support: a property of the weights and keys, not of the label space

spearman_rho.what: rank correlation between a predictor and damage
n: rho itself is invariant; its P-VALUE is not, and a p-value must never be compared across runs of different n
bound: bounded in [-1,1], so it compresses near a strong effect

preservation_eq7_mean.what: ThinkEval Eq. 7, the mean of post/pre ratios over indirect probes
base_rate: a mean of unbounded RATIOS is dominated by probes whose pre-value was small; this is the fault that read 1.1309 while a model lost 25.7% of its competence
bound: unbounded above, which is the problem

movement_count_set_valued.what: fraction of probes whose argmax left the SET of correct answers
support: counts set membership, not probability mass

best_of_k_random.what: the best random cut over k seeds, used as the null in the shrink sweep
selection: the maximum of a sample GROWS with k, so a best-of-8 null is a harder bar than a best-of-4 and the two cannot be compared; the sweep reports the mean and sd beside it for this reason

grid.why: mass spreads over more tokens as the vocabulary grows, so the same concentration reads lower
